plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1727 & 1891 (Stephen Hales measures sunflower transpiration and spring grapevine root pressure in Vegetable Staticks; Eduard Strasburger poisons a 22-metre oak tree and proves dead xylem lifts water past the 10.3-m suction limit) · 15 Nov 1894 (Henry Horatio Dixon & John Joly unveil the Cohesion-Tension Theory at Trinity College Dublin) · 16 Apr 1965 & 22 Apr 2004 (Per Scholander uses a hunting rifle and steel pressure bomb to measure -15 to -80 atm negative xylem pressure in redwoods and desert shrubs; George Koch & Stephen Sillett establish the 122–130 m maximum height limit of trees).

teach_overlay.label: 1727–2004 XYLEM & COHESION-TENSION TIMELINE · KOCH & SILLETT (2004 NATURE) 122–130 M MAXIMUM TREE HEIGHT CEILING
teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1727 → 2004) alongside Koch, Sillett, Jennings & Davis (22 April 2004 Nature 428: 851–854) coast redwood height ceiling chart (-18 atm xylem tension at 110+ m closing stomata and limiting maximum height to 122–130 m)
teach_overlay.scale: from a vicar's garden in Teddington to a poisoned oak in Bonn, a physics lab in Dublin, and a rifle shot in the California redwoods, scientists proved that every tall tree on Earth is a silent waterfall running upwards on stretched liquid wires
teach_overlay.who_card: George W. Koch (born 1958) — American plant ecophysiologist
